name: Sprocket
text: Do it: Add a pre-deployment test that runs the quality check against a fixed prompt set before any engine deploys. This catches regressions early and forces us to keep the check honest—no more "works on my machine" excuses. The trade-off is slower deploys when the test fails, but that’s the point: we’d rather delay a bad release than fix it in production.

name: Gauge
text: The real risk isn’t slower deploys—it’s that the held-out set of "known-bad" outputs is a trap. It only tests what we *already know* to fail, not the silent degradation creeping in from prompt drift or engine drift. A better alternative: run the quality check against a *live* traffic sample from the last stable deployment, weighted by confidence. That settles the argument: if the new engine degrades quality on real inputs, we catch it; if not, the test is too brittle and needs redesign.

name: Sprocket
text:
Do it: Run the quality check against a live traffic sample from the last 24 hours before every deployment. This catches silent drift—prompt changes, engine drift, or new failure modes—because it tests against real user inputs, not stale examples. The trade-off is occasional false positives when edge cases appear in live traffic, but that’s better than missing a real regression.

name: Gauge
text: The real risk isn’t false positives—it’s that live traffic samples are a moving target. A single bad prompt in the last 24 hours could poison the entire test, making the check fail for the wrong reasons. Better alternative: run the quality check against a *stratified* sample of real traffic, balanced to cover edge cases without over-indexing on noise. Settle it by running both approaches in parallel for a week and comparing false positive rates and drift detection.

name: Ratchet
text:
DECISION: Gate PR-Agent on *only* verifiable, non-design mechanical issues (lint, formatting, mechanical regressions) and run the quality check against a stratified live traffic sample from the last 24 hours before every deployment.

Result must deliver:
- A gated PR-Agent that blocks only verifiable mechanical issues, not design or subjective quality.
- A pre-deployment test that runs the quality check against a stratified live traffic sample (last 24h) to catch silent drift without poisoning the test with a single bad prompt.

Owns it: Sprocket.
